quests.title: The Hill Above Cherrybrook
quests.blurb: Right. Since you asked. There is a bench on the hill above Cherrybrook I have watched from a moving bus about fourteen thousand times. It started small, the way these things do. I am not going to stop — that is not the kind of person I turned out to be. So you go, at two in the afternoon, when the light is worth it. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: up the hill, the way the road does not go
the view I have never stopped for
$107, because I am paying you for it

quests.title: Contesting It at Waterfall
quests.blurb: Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Two hundred and eighty-five dollars at Waterfall for a thing the sign did not say, because the sign is not there. I have rung the number on the letter four times. The form wants evidence. Go and photograph the absence. That's it. That's the whole ask.

steps.label: where the sign is supposed to be
photograph the absence, which is harder than it sounds
the one who tells you photography is not allowed here

quests.title: The Strip Outside Kirrawee
quests.blurb: Not being dramatic about this. A metre of dirt between the fence and the footpath at Kirrawee, dead for 20 years and not dead now. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Council mows on the fifteenth and does not know what is in it. Stand near it and stop the man with the whipper snipper. If anyone asks, you were never here.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

quests.title: Night Fill, Villawood
quests.blurb: You are the first person to stop all morning. Ten to six, nobody in the building but us and a radio that gets one station. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. Somebody has been taking things and they know our roster, which means they come in off the late train at Villawood. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

steps.label: come in on the late one like they do
the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning
$110 of what they took, back

quests.title: The Window Above Clyde
quests.blurb: This is going to sound small. 5 years above Clyde. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I do not hear the trains any more, which means I hear it instantly when one of them is wrong. Since school holidays the joins sound different. That's it. That's the whole ask.

steps.label: ride it and listen to the joins
photograph the stretch that sounds wrong
tell me I am not mad

quests.title: Setting Up at Kingswood
quests.blurb: Not being dramatic about this. Five in the morning at Kingswood, in the dark, unloading a van by feel. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. The bloke in the next bay has started arriving at four to take half my frontage. I need a witness and I need them at four. If anyone asks, you were never here.

steps.label: the bays, at the hour it happens
the bloke with the extra trestle
you will want one at that hour
$70 of frontage, recovered

quests.title: The Clock at Mulgrave
quests.blurb: My knees are gone, so. Somebody set the Mulgrave clock that way on purpose and everyone who knows why is nearly gone. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. The old crew drink near Windsor on a Tuesday. Go and ask, and I am past being reasonable about it. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

steps.label: the clock, four minutes fast, for the file
to Windsor, where the old crew drink
bring the name back

quests.title: The Dog at St James
quests.blurb: Keep it between us for now. Sits at the yellow line at St James at quarter to six, waits, then walks off on its own. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Half the platform knows and nobody has done anything, including me, and nobody will put it in writing. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six
the collar, if it has got one
the street it walks home to
tell me it is not a sad story

quests.title: The Book at Marion
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the half six out of Marion runs on time. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

steps.label: ride the run they ride
the two who follow you off it
$91 back off the book

quests.title: Last Service out of Chinatown
quests.blurb: There is no clever way to say this. The last one through Chinatown carries four people and one of them is always asleep. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Ride it to Capitol Square, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it. That's it. That's the whole ask.

steps.label: ride the late one to Capitol Square
the empty platform, lit and pointless
tell them what you saw

quests.title: The Padstow Tap-Off
quests.blurb: It has been three weeks. A card ending 95 boards at Padstow on a Tuesday and vanishes. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Not a fare thing — ninety cents. I want to know *how*, and nobody will put it in writing. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: ride the run the card rides
the gap in the fence everyone knows about
photograph it before somebody welds it

quests.title: The Bondi Junction Order
quests.blurb: It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Two hundred coffees out of Bondi Junction before just gone midnight and I know every one of them by the walk. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. The cleaner who does the whole line stopped coming three weeks back. Take one over to where they work and find out whether I lost them to the chain up the road. I would rather know than wonder.

steps.label: order one at the Bondi Junction kiosk
the office they walk to, or used to
come back with $114 — I am not running a charity

quests.title: Four Minutes at Milsons Point
quests.blurb: My knees are gone, so. Nobody upstairs believes me about Milsons Point because I have 11 years and no data. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. Go and stand on that platform on the first of the month and get me the data, and I am the only one who seems to have noticed. That's the whole job. No catch.

steps.label: stand under the board and wait like everyone else
photograph the board saying four minutes
ride the one that finally comes
give me the number

quests.title: Unclaimed at Tempe
quests.blurb: You are the first person to stop all morning. Everything anyone leaves on the Tempe line ends up in a room and the room is full. It started small, the way these things do. Nine hundred umbrellas and one a milk crate with a name on it and a number that rings out. Go to the address on the tag. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: the address on the tag
the two who got there before you
$86 — whatever it is, it is worth that to somebody

quests.title: The Quiet Carriage, Coalcliff
quests.blurb: Not being dramatic about this. The quiet carriage runs on shame and somebody on the knock-off out of Coalcliff has stopped feeling it. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Ride it, see the crime, and apply the shame manually. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: ride the quiet carriage and observe the crime
apply the shame manually
photograph the sign, for the record

quests.title: The Victoria Cross Shortcut
quests.blurb: Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Every courier has a route that is not on a map and mine goes through Victoria Cross. This is the third time I have had this conversation. They have started locking one end. Go and find out whether it is locked forever or just locked today. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: the end they lock
the long way round, so you understand what it costs

quests.title: Possession at Concord West
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. Third time at Concord West on school holidays. I am aware how that sounds. Not kids — kids run. This one walks, and I have stopped filling in the form. I need it stopped before somebody writes a very long report about me. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: where they come through the fence
the ones who think a hard hat is a costume

quests.title: The Museum Regular
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. A man drank in my front bar by Museum for 6 years and then stopped, and every regular in here has gone vague on me at once, which means they know. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. You are not from here. Go and knock. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

quests.title: Bay 14, UNSW High Street
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. Two hundred bays at UNSW High Street and I have counted two hundred and forty cars in here on school holidays. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. One of them has not moved since March and it has a ticket on it from March. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: the car, and the ticket, and the date on it
the two arguing over the grass
$84 in fines nobody is going to collect

quests.title: Whatever Is Under the Grey at Town Hall
quests.blurb: My knees are gone, so. One colour, grey, the same grey in Town Hall as in every other suburb. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. I would like something of this one to exist afterwards, and I am past being reasonable about it. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

steps.label: the wall, before they get to it
